Lay out the islands

Source: R/layout.R
island_layout.Rd

The Açores are about 1,500 km west of the mainland and Madeira about 1,000 km to the south-west, so a map of Portugal drawn to scale is mostly ocean. get_map() and plot_pt() move the islands next to the mainland, as insets. island_layout() says how: which archipelagos to show, how to split them into insets, and whether to draw frames around them.

Usage

island_layout(
  both = "compact",
  raa = both,
  ram = both,
  frames = TRUE,
  box_position = "bottom_left"
)

Arguments

both

How to show both archipelagos: "compact", "groups", "box", "in_place" or "none". See Choices.

raa, ram

How to show the Açores (raa) or Madeira (ram), when it should differ from both: one of the choices, or a layout list (see Moving and resizing the islands section below).

frames

Draw frames around the insets? Only applies to archipelagos drawn as insets.

box_position

Where to put the rectangles, for "box": "bottom_left" or "top_left" of the mainland, or c(x, y), the longitude and latitude of the bottom-left corner of the stack.

Value

An island layout, to pass as islands to get_map() or plot_pt().

Details

Pass the result as islands to get_map() or plot_pt(). For the common cases a string is enough: islands = "none" is the same as islands = island_layout("none").

Choices

Each archipelago takes one of:

"compact"

(The default.) Insets arranged to take the least room: the Açores in four insets (the western group, the central group, São Miguel, and Santa Maria on its own), and Porto Santo in its own small inset, moved next to Madeira.

"groups"

The Açores in their three official groups (Ocidental, Central and Oriental). Madeira has no groups, so for Madeira this is the same as "compact".

"whole"

Madeira and Porto Santo in one inset, at their true distance apart. Not available for the Açores: at a size that fits next to the mainland, the smaller islands would be too small to read.

"box"

A labelled rectangle instead of the islands, stacked to the left of the mainland. Only works at levels where each archipelago is a single region: "nuts1", "nuts2", "nuts3" and "reg_saude". Can't be combined with insets.

"in_place"

The islands where they really are, without frames. The starting point for a map of one archipelago (see Examples).

"none"

Leave the archipelago out.

Frames

With frames = TRUE, get_map() adds the frames drawn around the insets, which show that the islands have been moved. They are extra rows with geopt_type = "frame", their name in geopt_label, and geopt_frame_level saying what they surround: 1 for a whole archipelago, 2 for a group of islands and 3 for a single island.

Moving and resizing the islands

island_layout() returns a list, which you can change before passing it on. Each archipelago drawn as insets has:

anchor

Longitude and latitude its insets are placed around.

label

The name on its frame (and on its rectangle, for "box").

frame_buffer

Space between the islands and the frame around the whole archipelago, in degrees.

groups

One entry per inset, each with:

crop

The part of the archipelago this inset shows, as c(xmin =, ymin =, xmax =, ymax =) in longitude and latitude. NULL shows the whole archipelago.

offset

Where the inset goes, as c(x, y) in degrees from anchor.

scale

How much to enlarge it. Default 1.

label

Optional. Draws a frame around this inset alone, with this name.

frame_level, frame_buffer

Optional. That frame's geopt_frame_level (default 3) and its space around the islands.

sub_frames

Optional. Frames around several insets at once, each with groups (the inset names), label, and optionally frame_buffer and frame_level (default 2).

Print island_layout()$raa to see a complete example. To lay out an archipelago from scratch, pass a list with the same structure as raa or ram.

See also

get_map(), plot_pt()

Examples

island_layout()
#> <island layout>
#>   raa (Açores):  compact   4 insets: ocidental, central, s_miguel, s_maria
#>   ram (Madeira):  compact   2 insets: madeira, porto_santo
#>   frames:         yes
island_layout(raa = "groups", ram = "whole")
#> <island layout>
#>   raa (Açores):  groups    3 insets: ocidental, central, oriental
#>   ram (Madeira):  whole     1 inset: madeira
#>   frames:         yes

get_map("municipio", islands = "none")    # mainland only

# The Açores alone, in their true position
m <- get_map("municipio", islands = "in_place")
acores <- m[m$nuts2_cod %in% "PT20", ]

# Move the Açores half a degree west, with an English label
lay <- island_layout()
lay$raa$anchor <- lay$raa$anchor + c(-0.5, 0)
lay$raa$label <- "Azores"
get_map("nuts3", islands = lay)
